title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This guide consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard processes for hiring, new-employee onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering and product leaders who run hiring programs and manage teams.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single, production-ready reference that reduces time-to-hire, improves new-hire ramp, and standardizes performance conversations across the company.
- Scope: Applies to all salaried US and EMEA employees (full-time and limited-term contractors >90 days). For Private/enterprise-specific contractors or security-sensitive roles, follow the additional guidance in Security & Compliance > rbac-and-auth.

High-level principles:
- Candidate experience first: transparent timelines, timely feedback, and clear expectations.
- Consistency: use standard scorecards and interview rubrics to reduce bias and improve calibration.
- Manager accountability: hiring managers own requisitions and onboarding outcomes; People Ops partners enable process and compliance.
- Data-driven: measure time-to-fill, offer-accept rates, new-hire 30/90-day retention, and ramp metrics.

1) Hiring process (standardized):
1.1 Requisition & approval
  - Manager identifies role and completes Hiring Requisition form (People Ops Jira HR-REQ template).
  - Required approvals: hiring manager, functional lead, finance (headcount), and People Ops.
  - SLA: approvals should complete within 3 business days.

1.2 Job posting & sourcing
  - Use standardized job descriptions from the Job Description library (link in related pages).
  - Sourcing channels: internal referral, LinkedIn Recruiter, partner agencies (pre-approved vendors list), and campus programs.
  - Commitment to diversity: ensure at least one diverse candidate in the final interview slate where possible.

1.3 Interview design
  - Standard interview loop for IC engineering roles: Recruiter screen (30m), Technical screen (45m), Take-home assignment (optional), On-site loop (4-5 interviews: System Design, Coding/Perf, Ownership & Product, Culture/Values, Final Hiring Manager).
  - Use the role-specific scorecard: areas scored (Technical Skill, System Design, Problem Solving, Ownership, Communication, Team Fit). Each interviewer submits a numerical score (1-5) and written rationale.
  - Interviewer training: all interviewers must complete the Interviewer Enablement training annually.

1.4 Decision & compensation
  - Hiring manager gathers scorecards and schedules a calibration meeting with People Ops to decide.
  - Offer recommendation includes target level, comp band, equity guidelines, and sign-on considerations. People Ops will verify budget and prepare the offer letter.
  - Target time from final interview to offer: 3 business days.

1.5 Offer acceptance & background check
  - People Ops sends offer and manages negotiation. Once accepted, People Ops triggers background check and sends the candidate pre-boarding checklist.
  - New hires must complete background checks and any role-specific security clearances before starting.

2) New-hire onboarding (30/60/90 framework):
Overview: Onboarding is a shared responsibility between hiring manager, IT/Infra, People Ops, and the new hire. The goal is to get employees to break-even contribution and confidence within 90 days, with explicit milestones at 30, 60, and 90 days.

2.1 Pre-boarding (completed by People Ops within 5 business days of offer acceptance)
  - Send welcome packet, first-day agenda, org chart, team handbook, and required forms (tax, direct deposit).
  - IT provisioning request: manager completes equipment and access form (laptop spec, monitor, additional hardware). SLA to fulfill provisioning: 5 business days.
  - Security & privacy training assigned before day 1 for roles touching customer data.

2.2 Day 1 checklist (owner: manager + People Ops)
  - Welcome meeting (30m) with manager.
  - Team introductions + buddy assignment.
  - Workspace & access verification: email, Slack, Jira, GitHub, Confluence, Redwood console demo account.
  - Mandatory trainings: Code of Conduct, Security Basics, Data Handling.

2.3 Week 1 deliverables
  - Complete developer environment setup (devbox, credentials, local build).
  - Shadowing sessions scheduled with cross-functional partners.
  - First-week OKRs: list 1-3 small deliverables (examples provided in templates section).

2.4 30/60/90 milestones (manager-owned checkpoints)
  - 30 days: administrative tasks complete, primary repo familiarity, first small deliverable complete, manager check-in (30-45m).
  - 60 days: increased ownership, contributor to regular sprint work, cross-team sync scheduled, mid-onboarding feedback form submitted.
  - 90 days: ramp assessment, calibration with People Ops, agree next-quarter goals and a development plan.

2.5 Buddy program & manager checklist
  - Buddy responsibilities (peer-level): daily check-ins for week 1, weekly check-ins weeks 2-12, environment troubleshooting, culture orientation, and a list of 10-15 starter tasks.
  - Manager responsibilities: create 90-day plan, schedule weekly 1:1s, provide feedback, facilitate introductions to key stakeholders, and ensure training completion.

3) Performance & feedback cycles:
3.1 Cadence
  - Weekly 1:1s (manager and direct report) — keep notes and action items in 1:1 doc.
  - Quarterly check-ins: written self-assessment + manager assessment focusing on outcomes & growth.
  - Annual review & calibration: performance rating, compensation cycle, and promotion decisions.

3.2 Evaluation framework
  - Ratings scale: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement.
  - Evaluation inputs: objective outcomes (OKRs), peer feedback, manager observations, and data (e.g., uptime, ticket resolution, PR throughput where applicable).

3.3 Promotion & leveling
  - Promotion cycle: managers submit promotion packet with examples of impact, competency mapping, and calibration notes. People Ops schedules calibration and approves comp adjustments.
  - Promotion timeline: typical turnaround 4-6 weeks from packet submission.

3.4 Compensation planning
  - Compensation cycles are annual; people-ops provides guidelines, comp bands, and market adjustments. Salary changes outside cycle require VP-level approval and justification.

3.5 Performance improvement (PIP) process
  - Trigger: sustained performance rated Needs Improvement over two consecutive quarters or a severe incident.
  - Steps: 1) Manager documents concerns and examples, 2) People Ops consults and approves PIP initiation, 3) PIP plan created with clear metrics and 30/60/90 checkpoints, 4) Regular weekly reviews and final assessment.
  - Outcomes: improvement, extension (rare), or termination. Decisions are coordinated with People Ops and Legal.

4) Manager playbook — hiring & onboarding responsibilities (quick reference):
- Before hiring: define role outcomes, level, and success metrics; complete requisition; partner with People Ops on sourcing strategy.
- During interviews: attend calibration, use scorecards, provide timely feedback, and prioritize candidate experience.
- Pre-start: finalize 90-day plan, confirm equipment & access, assign buddy.
- First 90 days: weekly 1:1s, clear milestones, frequent feedback, and a 90-day ramp assessment; escalate blockers to People Ops.

4.1 Manager checklist (compact)
  - Submit requisition: date _____
  - Interview panel scheduled: date _____
  - Offer approved and sent: date _____
  - New hire start date: _____
  - 1st week goals shared: date _____
  - 30/60/90 check-ins scheduled: dates _____

5) Templates & artifacts (copy from People Ops templates folder):
- Job description templates (IC Engineering, Product, Sales, Support)
- Interview scorecard (numeric + narrative fields)
- 30/60/90 onboarding plan template
- New hire checklist (IT & Access)
- 90-day ramp assessment form
- PIP template and success criteria table

6) Metrics & reporting:
- Core metrics tracked monthly by People Ops: time-to-fill (target 45 days), offer-accept rate (target >= 60%), new-hire retention 90-day (target >= 85%), manager satisfaction with onboarding (survey target >= 4/5).
- Quarterly People Ops business review includes headcount by org, open req backlog, and ramp time trends.

7) Compliance & security notes:
- For roles handling customer data or private deployments, ensure KBA and customer NDAs are completed pre-start.
- All hires must complete annual security training within 30 days of hire.

8) Common FAQs & escalation paths:
- If equipment is delayed >5 business days: contact IT Escalations (it-esc@redwood.com) and People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
- If an interview panel lacks calibration: raise to People Ops Recruiting Partner for re-evaluation before making an offer.
- For complex visa/work authorization questions: contact Legal (legal-immigration@redwood.com).

Appendices:
A. Example 30/60/90 onboarding plan (sample)
  - 30 days: "Onboarded, contributed to bugfix, presented learning to team"
  - 60 days: "Delivered feature supporting team OKR, reduced PR review turnaround"
  - 90 days: "Full sprint contributor, proposed improvement to infra, development plan agreed"

B. PIP success criteria (sample table)
| Area | Metric | Target | Owner |
| Ownership & Delivery | On-time delivery of assigned tickets | 90% on-time | Manager |
| Code Quality | PR review findings | <3 actionable review items per month | Manager |
| Communication | Stakeholder updates | Weekly summary updates to stakeholders | Manager |
